rv.q: But its strengths especially the courageous, ruggedly brilliant performances by Michael Cerveris and Donna Murphy - are far more haunting than the flaws are troubling.

That wounding impulse to abnegate both the love itself and the pain that comes with denial colors every scene of “LoveMusik,” an uneven but fascinating portrait of the corrosive relationship between Weill and his wife Lotte Lenya.
Any show, no matter how uneven, that includes such a moment can be forgiven much.
I found LoveMusik itself a strangely tired show—a missed opportunity to achieve something original and genuinely Brechtian with Kurt Weill’s.
The show is daring, indeed, but considering all the talent involved ultimately disappointing and rarely moving.

tn.cat: Best Featured Actor in a Musical

cn.t: Critics are divided on this Weill-Lenya bio-musical: most praise the luminous lead performances by Cerveris and Murphy and Prince's moody direction, but find the show itself sluggish and tedious despite its ambitious, grown-up approach.

vs.sum: The Samuel J. Friedman Theatre offers good sightlines with minimal obstructions and a well-raked mezzanine, ensuring a clear view from most seats. The sound quality is consistently praised, and the seating is comfortable with decent legroom. The theater's ambiance is enhanced by its elegant design following renovation, though facilities like restrooms are average, leading to some congestion during intermissions.

acc.note: Elevator to all levels. Built-in induction loop for t-coil hearing aids.
